utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will the Registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, case number IT-99-37-PT, the Prosecutor versus Nikola Sainovic and Dragoljub Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, may we have the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I appear for the Prosecution but I have general oversight of the case but the case is being dealt with substantially by Ms. Romano who sits beside me, Mr. Saxon, and Mr. Shin and they'll deal with most of the matters for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For the Defence? Appearances for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honour, my name is Toma Fila, and together with Zoran Jovanovic, an attorney from Belgrade, I appear for Nikola Sainovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honour, my name is Tomislav Visnjic and with my colleague, Vojislav Selezan, I appear for General Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have a number of matters to discuss today in this Status Conference. I'll start first with the preliminary motions. There is a motion filed by Ojdanic seeking compliance with Rule 66(A)(i) and I am to say that the Chamber will give its decision on that by Friday of this week. Then there is a preliminary motion filed by the accused Sainovic, however, the Ojdanic Defence has indicated that it will also file a preliminary motion within 30 days of the determination of its motion as to disclosure. The Chamber has this motion under consideration but it will -- seems sensible to deal with both matters at the same time. I turn now to the pre-trial preparation, Rule 66(A)(i) disclosure, subject to the resolution of the matters raised in the Ojdanic motion, it appears that this phase of the disclosure is complete. Rule 66(A)(ii) disclosure, I am advised that the parties have worked cooperatively and the 65 ter conference that was convened yesterday was successful in resolving most of the issues. Ms. Romano, are you the person who will speak on behalf of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, in some of the matters, yes, and in some of the matters, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you would bring us up to date on the relevant matters such as the number of witnesses on which I understand agreement has been reached and the disclosure matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if agreement has been reached but yesterday in the pre-trial, 65 ter conference, I just -- we just discussed in a preliminary way some estimate number of witnesses and court schedule and court time that we are working on but they are quite preliminary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I understand that. But let me tell you what I have been advised and you can say whether that's consistent with your understanding. For crime base witnesses live, a number between 20 and 25.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct. Our intention is to present one witness per site or maybe even less than that if a witness can cover two sites at the same time, live witness, that's our intention and that will amount to 20, 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That would be very good, yes. And crime base witnesses under Rule 92 bis, a number between 36 and 40.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We also discussed that in this matter, we are quite uncertain because we will discuss with the Defence and we will need the cooperation with the Defence. We intend to use transcripts, we intend to use 92 bis and that will be depending on how we will work with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Experts, 8?

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Yes, we have identified 7 experts, they are the ones that we used in the Milosevic case and we also forecast more experts but we haven't identified them so far. But we will in the time frame given -- notice to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's likely to be more than eight? You have seven from Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: We have 7 from Milosevic. I'm not in a position to advance right now how many more we will have but I'm sure that we will have a couple more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: International witnesses, a number between 10 and 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And insiders, 25 to 30.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And this gives a total of a number between 99 and 118 witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I just raise again the fact that this is quite preliminary and we are really working in a way that we can introduce matters to short the court time and that we will work very close with the Defence but that's our first work with numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And the estimate for the presentation of the Prosecution case, I have something written down but I'd prefer if you said it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Our estimate is between 3 to 4 months plus what the number of 92 bis crime base witness we will reach with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think that would be remarkable, yes. We need to set a date for the disclosure of the witness statements and I have in mind November 30th for the date for the disclosure of the witness statements and for the disclosure of the reports from the experts, November 30th, most of them you would have already.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: If I can clarify, Your Honour, yesterday I also raised issue that in -- to complete our disclosure obligations under 66(A)(i) and 68 and the reciprocal disclosure we will need at least until March of next year and we were looking into 65 ter filings and the pre-trial brief in April, May so when you -- when you refer to November 30, I just don't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That information is new to me. I wasn't aware that we were looking so far down the road because I was going to set a date for the pre-trial brief the end of January.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you can just give me one second to confer with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, and the senior legal officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Romano, I have concluded my conference before you have concluded yours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I've taken into account what you have said and we need to be as expeditious as possible. What I would do then is for the witness statements, the end of December and the same date for the disclosure of the expert reports subject to your seeking any extension of time for good cause and the pre-trial brief, the end of February. The reciprocal disclosure obligations need not necessarily be tied to the other dates that we are fixing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Neither the 68, I understand that. I would just like to raise a couple of other issues that we had in mind when we just pushed the date to April or end of April. First is the preliminary motions that are still standing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes but those will be dealt with by the end of this week, you will have -- one will be disposed of and -- what the Chamber has in mind is to fix in its decision a date for all motions to be filed and dealt with, perhaps within a month of that. So I don't anticipate that will hold us up too long.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: We are right now in the date of end of December for the statements. The other issue that I would raise was that we were intending to discuss this with the Defence and to seek manners on how to present including the crime base evidence in a more expeditious way and with the transcripts we need to just discuss with them or portions, large portions of the transcript or anything that we can get agreement, common agreements on and that can take some time and that will help to shorten the time in court and presentation of the case. That's what we had in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You should still go ahead with that but I'd still like to maintain the schedule that I just outlined, work towards that schedule.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: We will do our best and I think we are in a good position to start disclosing statements but I would like to have some time to work on -- with the Defence on common points. One more matter that could affect the time table would be the surrender of the last accused, that is listed in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, well if that arises that's an eventuality that we'll have to deal with. Is there any other matter that the Prosecutor wishes to raise before I call on the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just one matter that Mr. Nice will raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Interviewing of the accused is a problem. There were various protestations made at the application for the provisional release about the willingness of the accused to be interviewed. That willingness and those protestations have somewhat changed and so that they are now said to be contingent on the granting of provisional release and interviews that are only available in Belgrade. Of course it's a matter for the accused whether they wish to be interviewed or are prepared to be interviewed, we accept that. But in identifying issues for this case, and examining now or in due course the attitude of the accused towards these proceedings, the earlier the interviews take place the better from everyone's point of view. One of the accused has said that he's only been in a position to consider being interviewed when there's been full disclosure well that's not exactly the way it always works. There's been a great deal of cooperation between my colleagues and the Defence in relation to disclosure and disclosure is proceeding as is recorded by the Defence in a very satisfactory way but accused don't necessarily wait or expect to wait until the very last minute before they are interviewed, interviewing is frequently part of the process. So we are to a degree unhappy to see that interviewing is being postponed and said now to be contingent on the granting of provisional release. Anything that can be done to encourage or assist the process of interviewing the accused will assist us generally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's not essentially a matter for the Chamber. I think you have to work as cooperatively as you can with the parties and you have been working cooperatively.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I expect that that cooperation will continue but I wouldn't want to be intervening in the application of Rule 63, if a legal issue arises and the Chamber is asked to rule on it then we'll do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. There is -- I'm grateful to Ms. Romano, there is one other matter that I thought I'd mention: Under reciprocal disclosure, materials coming to us, we should recall that we are going to deal with that so far as any other case in the Tribunal is concerned in the same way as any other material coming to us. Thus, if that material is material that has to be disclosed to other accused in other cases, that will be done. It doesn't fall into any separate category simply because it's material coming to us by way of a reciprocal disclosure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, allow me to say that one of the obligations I undertook in -- on behalf of Mr. Sainovic when he was provisionally released and the same applies for General Ojdanic was that they should be interviewed in Belgrade after their release. I accepted this and my client signed a statement to that effect as did I. I fail to understand now why Mr. Nice is raising this issue. This is the second timing it's been raised. The first time by Mr. Kevin Curtis who threatened us by saying that Mr. Nice would inform the Chamber of this. I don't know whether this was meant to frighten me or not, but I don't know why this is being raised now. On Friday, four days ago, the OTP adduced us with their motion appealing Your Honour's decision on provisional release. Had this process not been slowed down in this way, we would now have an appeals decision and I would be able to tell you whether the interview would take place here or in Belgrade as we agreed. So it is only Mr. Nice's team that is to blame for this waste of time it's not the Defence. As for the deadline set by Your Honour, we have two problems. The first one is connected to Rule 65 ter E, which says that once any existing preliminary motions filed within the time limit provided by Rule 72 are disposed of and so on. How can you resolve something that has not been submitted? The preliminary motion has not yet been written. It has not been submitted, it is only after it has been submitted that you can reach a decision on it and only then will the conditions be met for us to discuss what we are discussing now and to set time limits. I think that Ms. Romano's wish should be agreed to and that it should be in April or May next year. Let me say that on the 4th of January, Mr. Milutinovic's mandate expires, his term of office expires and he is then duty-bound to turn up in The Hague. He is duty-bound to do that he has to do it. It's not something he can decide about, it's an obligation undertaken by Yugoslavia and a representative of the ministry of justice testified to this. However, Your Honour, I wish to express my fear that this will additionally slow us down because anything that Mr. Visnjic and I agreed to with the Prosecution also has to be agreed to by Mr. Milutinovic's Defence. That's why perhaps it's better for us to wait for January to pass and then we will have another team involved in the proceedings and we can all sit down together and discuss how to expedite these proceedings. However we agree with Ms. Romano that the proceedings should be expedited and we have no problems with the number of witnesses or the time limits. However, I think it would be wise to wait for Mr. Milutinovic's surrender in January in order to fix the dates. That's all I have to say, I apologise for taking so long. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Fila. Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will be very brief. I will first refer to what Mr. Nice said about General Ojdanic's possible interview. Mr. Nice spoke in a very generalised manner but we made our position clear from the very beginning and that was that our client would speak to the OTP when he had received enough material to enable him to talk to them in a useful way. So this is not some sort of condition that we are now imposing. Our stance has been the same from the very beginning. As for the time limits and our cooperation, I wish to say that we have started reciprocal discovery with the OTP and that we have fulfilled our obligations under Rule 67. Yesterday, we discussed various time limits but our understanding was that these time limits can be maintained only after thorough preparations on both sides. Unfortunately, the time limits Your Honour has now stated do not make it possible for us to prepare as thoroughly as we discussed with the OTP yesterday and the previous conferences and therefore, I agree with the remarks made by my colleague, Mr. Fila, that is to say that when we have received more material and have a clearer picture of the intentions of the OTP and the volume of material to be disclosed, it is then that we can settle these issues. I think there will be another technical problem and that concerns the translation of certain materials. I will try to clarify this with the Registry within the next few days and after that, we will be able to take up a position as regards the time limits set by Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have listened to the representations made both by Mr. Fila and Mr. Visnjic and also to a certain extent by Ms. Romano and in light of that, I'm going to move the dates one month later so that for the witness statements, the end of January, the disclosure of the expert reports end of January, and the pre-trial brief the end of March. I'll ask the senior legal officer to assist me with fixing the date for the next Status Conference. Is there any other matter before I return to that particular question? Well let me call on the accused, Mr. Sainovic. Will you stand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SAINOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is there anything you wish to raise regarding the case in general or regarding the conditions of your detention?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SAINOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED OJDANIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no special issues to raise because any problems that arise are resolved very well with the administration of the detention unit. I hope you will not misunderstand me but the only issue I would wish to raise is that the food is not in accordance with our habits and culture in our country. The expenses are great, but 80 per cent of what we receive is thrown away and then we have to spend our money in the canteen. This is probably not something that this Court is competent for but we shall apply in writing to the administration of the detention unit in order to try to find a satisfactory solution. I have no other issues. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ojdanic and the matter that you mentioned regarding food I will ask the Registrar to bring that to the attention of the head of the detention unit and have it investigated and dealt with. The senior legal officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The date for the next Status Conference is Wednesday, February 12th at 3 p.m. Is there any other matter? There being none, the hearing stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: at 3.40 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 12th day of February, 2003, at 3 p.m.
